mcqs.question: A metal block is subjected to forces acting parallel to its top surface, causing its layers to slide over each other. Which type of stress is primarily produced in the block?
mcqs.explanation: When forces act parallel to a surface causing adjacent layers to slide, the internal restoring force per unit area is shear or tangential stress. Longitudinal stress acts along the length, bulk stress is uniform in all directions, and tensile stress is a type of longitudinal stress under pulling.

mcqs.question: If a force of 200 N is applied uniformly over an area of 0.02 m², the internal restoring force per unit area is called:
mcqs.explanation: Stress is defined as the internal restoring force per unit area, mathematically σ = F/A. Strain is deformation per unit length, pressure is force per area in fluids, and modulus of elasticity relates stress to strain.

mcqs.question: A student writes that stress equals force multiplied by area (σ = F×A). Which expression correctly gives stress?
mcqs.explanation: The correct definition of stress is force divided by the area over which it acts (σ = F/A). Multiplying force by area gives a quantity with units of N·m², which is not stress. The other options are also incorrect formulations.

mcqs.question: A steel rod is pulled at both ends along its length. Which type of stress is primarily experienced by the rod?
mcqs.explanation: Pulling a material along its length creates normal stress acting parallel to the axis, known as longitudinal (or normal) stress. Tangential stress acts parallel to a surface, bulk stress is uniform in all directions, and hydrostatic stress applies to fluids under pressure.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes bulk stress from longitudinal and tangential stresses?

options.A: Bulk stress acts uniformly in all directions within a material under pressure, while longitudinal stress acts along the length and tangential stress acts parallel to a surface.
options.B: Bulk stress is the same as longitudinal stress but occurs only in solids.
options.C: Bulk stress occurs only in fluids and is unrelated to stresses in solids.
options.D: Bulk stress is measured in newtons per meter, unlike other stresses measured in pascals.

mcqs.answer: Bulk stress acts uniformly in all directions within a material under pressure, while longitudinal stress acts along the length and tangential stress acts parallel to a surface.
mcqs.explanation: Bulk (or hydrostatic) stress is isotropic, acting equally in all directions, typical of fluids or solids under uniform pressure. Longitudinal stress is normal to the cross‑section along the length, and tangential (shear) stress acts parallel to a surface. Options B, C, and D contain inaccurate descriptions.

mcqs.question: A rectangular steel bar of cross‑section 10 mm × 20 mm is subjected to a force of 5 kN acting parallel to its larger face. What is the magnitude of the tangential stress produced?
mcqs.explanation: Area = 10 mm × 20 mm = 200 mm² = 2 × 10⁻⁴ m². Stress = Force/Area = 5000 N / 2 × 10⁻⁴ m² = 2.5 × 10⁷ Pa = 25 MPa. Hence option A is correct. The other options correspond to incorrect area or force calculations.

mcqs.question: Stress is best defined as:
mcqs.explanation: Stress is the internal restoring force per unit area (σ = F/A). Deformation per unit length is strain, energy per unit volume is energy density, and rate of change of momentum relates to force, not stress.

mcqs.question: A force of 120 N acts uniformly on a surface area of 0.03 m². What is the stress produced?
mcqs.explanation: Stress σ = F/A = 120 N / 0.03 m² = 4000 N/m². Option C matches this calculation. The other options result from misplaced decimal placement or incorrect division.
